BodyText: OAI’s investigation established that a firm and an individual engaged in fraudulent practices by misrepresenting a joint venture arrangement and the consent of a proposed expert, including the use of the expert’s curriculum vitae, in a proposal submitted for an ADB-financed contract. ADB’s Integrity Enforcement Committee concurred with OAI’s findings and debarred the firm and its chairman for a minimum period of three years for engaging in fraudulent practices.

An OAI investigation established that a firm violated an ADB debarment and engaged in a fraudulent practice by participating in the bidding for, and winning, an ADB-financed contract while debarred and by misrepresenting in its bid submission that it was not debarred. The firm entered into a Proposed Resolution Agreement (PRA) with OAI, under which it accepted responsibility for the integrity violations and accepted a debarment for a minimum period of three years. The debarment, which became effective upon consent of the Chair of the Integrity Enforcement Committee, is published and extends to the affiliates of Jiangneng Company. Reinstatement is subject to compliance with specified conditions, including the (i) adoption and effective implementation of integrity-related policies and procedures, (ii) written protocols to prevent similar integrity violations, and (iii) integrity training for staff and management.

An OAI investigation established that a firm, while acting as the tendering agent for an ADB-financed consulting contract, engaged in fraudulent practice by failing to disclose a conflict of interest arising from its relationship with a bidder participating in the procurement. The nondisclosure undermined the integrity and transparency of the selection process and resulted in the rebidding of the contract and delays in project implementation. The firm accepted OAI’s findings and the proposed four-year debarment with conditional reinstatement. Reinstatement is subject to compliance with specified conditions, including the (i) adoption and effective implementation of integrity-related policies and procedures, (ii) written protocols to prevent similar integrity violations, and (iii) integrity training for staff and management. Compliance with these conditions is subject to verification by an independent compliance monitor acceptable to OAI. While debarred, the firm and their related entities are ineligible to participate in any ADB-related activities.

OAI’s investigation found that a firm engaged in fraudulent practices by submitting forged documents relating to its previous experience in support of its bid for an ADB-financed contract in Cambodia. These false documents were included to mislead the executing agency that the firm had complied with the bid requirements of the bid. ADB’s Integrity Enforcement Committee concurred with OAI’s findings and debarred the firm for four years for engaging in fraudulent practices.

OAI’s investigation established that a firm and an individual engaged in fraudulent practices by: (i) misrepresenting ST’s Average Annual Construction Turnover (AACT), balance sheets, income statements, and financial statements, submitted in response to the EA’s request for clarification following its submission of the bid; and (ii) failing to disclose pending litigation in a bid for an ADB-financed contract in Uzbekistan. ADB’s Integrity Enforcement Committee concurred with OAI’s findings and debarred the firm and its chief executive officer and director for four years for engaging in fraudulent practices.
